questions.question: The candidate's resume was filled with ________ accomplishments; upon closer background scrutiny, several of the celebrated corporate turnarounds proved to be completely fabricated.
questions.explanation: 'Apocryphal' means of doubtful authenticity, although widely circulated as being true. The clue 'proved to be completely fabricated' directly establishes that the claims were spurious and not genuine.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Advanced Vocabulary

questions.question: Far from being ________ to new technological innovations, the conservative manufacturing firm eagerly adopted robotic welding lines to outpace international competitors.
questions.explanation: 'Far from being [blank]' signals an opposition to 'eagerly adopted'. 'Inimical' means hostile or adverse. Being far from hostile means they were receptive.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Text Completion

questions.question: Although the author attempted to present a (i)________ evaluation of the controversial trial, critics condemned the monograph as fundamentally (ii)________, noting that it systematically suppressed evidence favorable to the defense.
questions.explanation: 'Although' sets up a contrast between the intended presentation ('dispassionate' = neutral, objective) and the actual condemned result ('tendentious' = expressing a strong, biased point of view).
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Multi-Blank Text Completion

questions.question: The theoretical physicist found herself frustrated by the (i)________ nature of the cosmological data, which proved so ambiguous that it could be cited to (ii)________ virtually any competing hypothesis.
questions.explanation: 'Proved so ambiguous' indicates the data was 'equivocal' (open to more than one interpretation). Because it was vague, researchers could use it to 'corroborate' (confirm or give support to) almost any competing view.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Context Clues

questions.question: Historians long regarded the monarch as (i)________ ruler whose reign was characterized by indolence; however, recent archival discoveries reveal a monarch who was remarkably (ii)________, working tirelessly behind the scenes to (iii)________ administrative corruption.
options: Blank (i): a feckless | Blank (ii): industrious | Blank (iii): extirpate
Blank (i): a dynamic | Blank (ii): lethargic | Blank (iii): perpetuate
Blank (i): a visionary | Blank (ii): torpid | Blank (iii): entrench
Blank (i): an omnipotent | Blank (ii): capricious | Blank (iii): foment
Blank (i): a despotic | Blank (ii): indolent | Blank (iii): condone
questions.explanation: Blank 1 matches 'indolence' -> 'feckless' (lacking initiative or strength of character). 'However... working tirelessly' contrasts with indolence -> Blank 2 is 'industrious'. Working tirelessly against corruption -> Blank 3 is 'extirpate' (root out and destroy completely).
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Triple Blank Completion

questions.question: The diplomat's negotiating style was notoriously ________; he rarely made direct statements, preferring evasive circumlocutions that kept counterparts in perpetual suspense.
questions.explanation: 'Tortuous' means excessively lengthy and complex, devious, or indirect. The clue 'rarely made direct statements, preferring evasive circumlocutions' directly matches 'tortuous'.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — GRE Vocabulary

questions.question:
Sentence: 'The archaeological excavation yielded evidence that was decidedly ________; while ceramic shards suggested an expansive mercantile hub, the complete absence of defensive walls confounded military historians.'

Select the two words that produce sentences with the most equivalent meaning:
questions.explanation: The contrast between an expansive trade hub and the lack of defensive fortifications is unexpected and contradictory. Both 'anomalous' (deviating from standard) and 'paradoxical' (seemingly contradictory) create coherent, equivalent sentences.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Sentence Equivalence

questions.question:
Sentence: 'Critics accused the new mayor of ________, noting that despite campaign promises of fiscal discipline, she allocated lavish subsidies to pet municipal projects.'

Select the two words that produce sentences with the most equivalent meaning:
questions.explanation: The context contrasts promised 'fiscal discipline' with allocating 'lavish subsidies'. Both 'profligacy' and 'extravagance' denote wasteful, reckless spending of resources.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Sentence Equivalence

questions.question:
Sentence: 'The researcher’s presentation was so dense with jargon and disorganized data that it served only to ________ an already intricate subject.'

Select the two words that produce sentences with the most equivalent meaning:
questions.explanation: Being dense with jargon and disorganized data serves to make things harder to understand. Both 'obfuscate' and 'bewilder' mean to make obscure, unclear, or confused.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Sentence Equivalence

questions.question:
Sentence: 'Even after hours of aggressive cross-examination, the defendant remained completely ________, answering every inquiry in a calm, flat monotone.'

Select the two words that produce sentences with the most equivalent meaning:
questions.explanation: Answering in a 'calm, flat monotone' despite aggressive questioning describes emotional detachment and calmness. Both 'impassive' and 'phlegmatic' denote showing no emotion and remaining composed.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Sentence Equivalence

questions.question:
Passage: 'For over a century, neuroscientists adhered to the dogma that the adult mammalian central nervous system was fixed and immutable, incapable of generating new neurons after critical developmental windows closed. However, the discovery of adult neurogenesis in the subgranular zone of the dentate gyrus fundamentally revised neural plasticity models. Far from being a static computational circuit, the adult brain dynamically integrates newly generated granular cells into existing hippocampal memory networks, demonstrating that cognitive decline is mediated by environmental and molecular modulators rather than inexorable structural arrest.'

The primary purpose of the passage is to:
options: Describe a scientific paradigm shift from neural immutability to dynamic adult plasticity
Argue that neurogenesis can completely eliminate Alzheimer's disease
Demonstrate that early childhood development is irrelevant to adult memory
Criticize the experimental methodologies of 19th-century neuroanatomists
questions.explanation: The passage outlines the older dogma of adult neural immutability, introduces the discovery of adult neurogenesis in the hippocampus, and explains how this revised our understanding of brain plasticity.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Primary Purpose

questions.question: Based on the neurogenesis passage in Q31, it can be reasonably inferred that the historical view of the adult brain was:
options: Overly deterministic in assuming that neural structure was permanently locked after early development
Completely unaware of the existence of the hippocampus
Rooted in the belief that environmental modulators stimulated excessive brain growth
Premised on the notion that neurons divide through continuous systemic mitosis
questions.explanation: The author notes that older dogma treated the adult brain as 'fixed and immutable' and assumed 'inexorable structural arrest', meaning it was overly deterministic about developmental finality.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Inferential Reasoning

questions.question:
Argument: 'A tech startup developed an AI algorithm that achieved a 98% accuracy score in identifying malignant melanoma lesions from high-resolution digital photographs in laboratory trials. The founders conclude that deploying this app directly to smartphone users will drastically reduce late-stage melanoma mortality.'

Which of the following is an unstated assumption required by the founders' conclusion?
options: Amateur smartphone camera images taken by users will provide sufficient resolution and lighting comparable to lab conditions
Malignant melanoma is the only form of skin cancer that poses a threat to public health
Dermatologists will universally oppose the adoption of automated diagnostic tools
The cost of cloud computing will remain constant over the next five years
questions.explanation: The argument moves from laboratory trials with high-resolution photos to user-taken smartphone photos. The conclusion holds only if everyday user photos have adequate quality for the AI algorithm to maintain its diagnostic accuracy.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Critical Reasoning: Assumptions

questions.question: Argument (Continued from Q33): Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the founders' claim that the app will reduce melanoma mortality?
options: False-positive results prompt thousands of anxious users with benign moles to inundate clinics, crowding out and delaying high-risk patients who actually have malignant lesions
Melanoma accounts for less than five percent of all skin cancer cases diagnosed annually
Smartphones require periodic lithium battery recharging
Older dermatologists possess more clinical diagnostic experience than medical interns
questions.explanation: If widespread false positives flood clinics and delay appointments for true melanoma patients, the app inadvertently increases mortality by causing treatment delays for actual cases.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Critical Reasoning: Weaken

questions.question:
Passage: 'Proponents of geoengineering tout stratospheric aerosol injection as an effortless silver bullet against global heating. Yet their techno-utopian rhetoric willfully glosses over the catastrophic peril of termination shock—should an injection program halt abruptly due to geopolitical conflict, decades of suppressed thermal forcing would rebound within months, triggering climatic convulsions far more violent than the steady warming it was designed to mask.'

The author's tone toward stratospheric aerosol injection can best be described as:
questions.explanation: Phrases like 'techno-utopian rhetoric willfully glosses over', 'catastrophic peril of termination shock', and 'climatic convulsions far more violent' convey deep skepticism and urgent apprehension.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Author Tone

questions.question: According to the passage in Q35, 'termination shock' refers to:
options: The rapid, catastrophic thermal rebound that occurs if an ongoing aerosol injection program is suddenly discontinued
The sudden failure of agricultural crops in equatorial regions due to cooling
The psychological shock experienced by climate researchers
The economic bankruptcy of geoengineering aerospace contractors
questions.explanation: The text directly defines termination shock: 'should an injection program halt abruptly due to geopolitical conflict, decades of suppressed thermal forcing would rebound within months'.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Textual Evidence

questions.question:
Paradox: 'In 2023, City X replaced its standard traffic intersections with modern multilane roundabouts. Although the total number of minor fender-bender vehicle collisions increased by 15%, the number of fatal and severe-injury traffic collisions plummeted by over 70%.'

Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?
options: Roundabouts force vehicles to travel at lower speeds in the same direction, virtually eliminating high-speed head-on and perpendicular T-bone impacts while increasing low-speed side-swipes
City X experienced slightly higher rainfall than neighboring municipalities during the autumn months
The municipal budget for road resurfacing was increased by five percent
Pedestrians prefer walking on sidewalks equipped with streetlamps
questions.explanation: This explains both sides of the paradox: low speeds and same-direction flow eliminate lethal perpendicular/head-on crashes (causing severe injuries to plummet 70%), while merging maneuvers cause more minor low-speed sideswipes (accounting for the 15% increase in fender-benders).
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Resolving Paradoxes

questions.question:
Argument: 'Paleoanthropologists hypothesize that early hominins began cooking food around 1.8 million years ago, which facilitated brain expansion by drastically reducing the digestive energy required to extract nutrients from raw meat and tubers.'

Which of the following, if true, provides the strongest support for this hypothesis?
options: Fossil records show that Homo erectus evolved significantly smaller gut volumes and smaller teeth alongside rapidly expanding cranial capacities around 1.8 million years ago
Modern humans consume processed sugar in greater quantities than ancestral foragers
Chimpanzees in equatorial Africa occasionally use sticks to dig for termites
Fire burns at different temperatures depending on the moisture of the wood
questions.explanation: A smaller gut and smaller teeth provide direct morphological evidence that diet became softer and easier to digest (a hallmark of cooked food), supporting the link between cooked food and metabolic reallocation toward brain growth.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Strengthening Arguments

questions.question:
Passage Sentence: 'The corporate board’s decision to liquidate the manufacturing subsidiary was widely seen as an expedient maneuver to placate vocal institutional investors before the quarterly earnings report.'

In this context, 'expedient' most nearly means:
options: Politically or practically advantageous, though perhaps unprincipled
Hasty and conducted without legal counsel
questions.explanation: 'Expedient' means convenient and practical, although possibly improper or unprincipled. The context shows it was done to quickly appease shareholders before reporting.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Contextual Meaning

questions.question:
Passage: 'Philosopher Karl Popper famously argued that scientific theories can never be verified, only falsified. Consider the claim that all swans are white: observing a million white swans cannot logically prove the claim, whereas observing a single black swan instantly refutes it. Critics argue, however, that real scientific practice rarely discards promising paradigms based on isolated recalcitrant observations; instead, researchers initially scrutinize instrumentation error.'

The author mentions the 'black swan' observation primarily in order to:
options: Provide an illustrative concrete example of Popper's asymmetry between verification and falsification
Demonstrate that ornithology is the most empirically rigorous branch of biology
Prove that Karl Popper's philosophy of science was entirely mistaken
Argue that European explorers had never traveled to Australia before the 17th century
questions.explanation: The black swan analogy is introduced directly after the claim that 'theories can never be verified, only falsified' to illustrate how one counterexample can decisively disprove a universal hypothesis.
questions.citation: Official ETS GRE Verbal Reasoning Framework — Rhetorical Functions
